You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    tc.id,
    tc.series_name,
    tc.Country,
    tc.Language
FROM TV_Channel AS tc
JOIN Cartoon AS c
    ON tc.id = c.Channel;
```
I need to find out which countries the tv channels are from.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    tc.Country
FROM TV_Channel AS tc
JOIN Cartoon AS c
    ON tc.id = c.Channel
WHERE tc.Country IS NOT NULL;
```
I need to check if the tv channels are currently airing the cartoons.

The schema doesn’t include a “currently airing” or schedule/status field, so the closest check is whether a cartoon’s `Original_air_date` is today.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    tc.Country
FROM TV_Channel AS tc
JOIN Cartoon AS c
    ON tc.id = c.Channel
WHERE tc.Country IS NOT NULL
  AND DATE(c.Original_air_date) = CURRENT_DATE;
```
I also want to confirm that the cartoons being shown are written by Todd Casey.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
    tc.Country,
    tc.id AS channel_id,
    tc.series_name AS channel_name,
    c.Title AS cartoon_title,
    c.Written_by
FROM TV_Channel AS tc
JOIN Cartoon AS c
    ON tc.id = c.Channel
WHERE tc.Country IS NOT NULL
  AND DATE(c.Original_air_date) = CURRENT_DATE
  AND c.Written_by LIKE '%Todd Casey%';
```
